claims.head: Best on best: Suzuki against Benson
claims.call: The Canadiens’ L1 (Suzuki, Caufield and Slafkovský) spends at least 42% of its 5-on-5 time against the Sabres’ first line.
claims.body: At home, the Canadiens keep sending Suzuki’s line (Suzuki, Caufield and Slafkovský) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Martin St. Louis has been choosing strength on strength. Tonight the Sabres’ first line is Quinn, Östlund and Benson.
claims.nums: At home: 42% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against first lines, about 32% with no line matching
claims.gist: At home, Martin St. Louis likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Sabres’ first line.

claims.head: The Canadiens come in rested
claims.body: It’s the Sabres’ second game in two nights. Teams on the back end of those usually spend more time defending, so we think the Canadiens get more of the play than usual.
claims.call: The Canadiens get a bigger share of the 5-on-5 chances than they usually do.

notes.text: R. Dahlin is day to day (upper body injury), reported after he played in their last game. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
J. Zucker is on injured reserve (abdomen surgery) and has not played this season.
Z. Metsa has started killing penalties: on the ice for 53% of the team’s shorthanded time in 6 games, up from 7% last season.
J. Norris has started killing penalties: on the ice for 34% of the team’s shorthanded time in 6 games, up from 1% last season.
I. Demidov is on injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 3 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. K. Dach has taken his spot beside A. Newhook and J. Slafkovský.
M. Matheson is day to day (lower body injury), reported after he played in their last game. He is a top-pair defenseman.
K. Guhle returned in their last game after missing 4 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.

MTL.head: Montréal starts a half-step ahead
MTL.body: Even though Buffalo has been out-chancing opponents lately, while Montréal will be without Demidov, Buffalo is on the second night of a back-to-back and may be without Dahlin, while Montréal has home-ice advantage. Buffalo can still swing it if they get good looks.

BUF.head: A slightly uphill night for Buffalo
BUF.body: Even though Buffalo has been out-chancing opponents lately, while Montréal will be without Demidov, Buffalo is on the second night of a back-to-back and may be without Dahlin, while Montréal has home-ice advantage. Buffalo’s best way to tip it is getting good looks.

items.text: Alex Lyon is on injured reserve (upper-body injury) and has not played this season. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen is expected to start.
Nick Suzuki has a point in eight straight games against Buffalo, and 20 points in his last twelve against them.
Rasmus Dahlin is day to day (upper body injury) and missed their last game. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
